comment: Runtime contract for scripts/runtime.py. Nothing here is a secret; safe to commit.
interpreters decides how a stage is launched: a per-machine python binary (venv or absolute path) or a conda env name.
profiles are memory/time budgets, not quality claims. 'full' mirrors docs; 'low'/'tiny' are the no-OOM ladder for laptops.

interpreters._prefer_comment: auto | venv | conda | system. 'auto' uses venv/overrides when present, else conda env names, else the running interpreter.

comment: expandable_segments cuts allocator fragmentation, which matters most on 6-8 GiB GPUs.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES / OMP_NUM_THREADS can be injected per run with --gpus and --threads.

auto_profile.comment: When --profile auto: no CUDA -> tiny; else pick by the free-GPU-memory threshold that matches.

full.comment: As documented in README/DATASETS. Needs a real CUDA workstation.

low.comment: 8 GiB-class GPU: fewer frames, bf16 backbone, quarter-res images, small Gaussian budget.

tiny.comment: Integrated graphics / CPU / CI smoke: 3 frames, tiny images, tens of steps. Proves plumbing only.
